messages.content:
The `WordUtils.abbreviate` method in the `org.apache.commons.lang.WordUtils` class takes a string `str`, lower and upper limits for abbreviation, and an optional string to append at the end. The method adjusts the upper limit to the length of the string if it is greater than the string length, but it does not adjust the lower limit. If lower is greater than the length of the string, it causes `StringIndexOutOfBoundsException` on the `str.substring(0, upper)` line.

Given the bug report, it seems that the lower value should also be adjusted to the length of the string. This adjustment is missing in the implementation of the `abbreviate` method, causing the bug when lower is greater than the length of the string.

I will now provide a step-by-step diagnosis of the bug.
Title: Diagnosis
Details: The bug occurs in the `WordUtils.abbreviate` method of the `org.apache.commons.lang.WordUtils` class. The method adjusts the upper limit to the length of the input string if it exceeds the length. However, it fails to adjust the lower limit accordingly. This results in a scenario where if the lower limit is greater than the length of the string, the upper limit will also be too large, leading to a `StringIndexOutOfBoundsException` when trying to abbreviate the string.

The fix for this issue is to adjust the lower limit to the length of the string to ensure it does not exceed the string's length. This adjustment will prevent the upper limit from becoming invalid and causing the exception.

The behavior observed in the code snippet matches the symptoms described in the bug report, confirming that the missing adjustment of the lower limit is the likely root cause of the bug.

I will now suggest the methods that need to be fixed to resolve this issue.

Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
